name: pmacct
what_it_is: pmacct is a multi-purpose passive network monitoring suite that collects IP traffic accounting data via libpcap, NetFlow/IPFIX, sFlow, and NFLOG, while also collecting BGP, BMP, and Streaming Telemetry control-plane data. It correlates data-plane flows with control-plane BGP/BMP information and exports to multiple backends including Kafka, AMQP, SQL databases, and flat files.
components: pmacctd — libpcap-based packet accounting daemon; can also export via NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow
nfacctd — NetFlow v5/v9 and IPFIX collector daemon; supports replication to third-party collectors
sfacctd — sFlow v2/v4/v5 collector daemon; supports replication
uacctd — Linux Netlink NFLOG accounting daemon; can export via NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow
pmbgpd — standalone BGP collector daemon; acts as passive iBGP/eBGP neighbor, maintains per-peer RIBs
pmbmpd — standalone BMP (BGP Monitoring Protocol) collector daemon
pmtelemetryd — standalone Streaming Telemetry collector; supports TCP/UDP/gRPC/gNMI input
pmacct — CLI client for querying memory-table plugin; outputs formatted/CSV/JSON
measurement: Per-flow IP traffic accounting: src/dst host, src/dst port, protocol, bytes, packets
BGP RIB table dumps at configurable intervals (bgp_table_dump_refresh_time)
BMP adjacent-RIB-in metrics with peer IP, AS path, communities, prefixes
Streaming Telemetry collection: interface counters, platform metrics via OpenConfig/Cisco/Huawei YANG
Traffic classification via nDPI deep packet inspection (--enable-ndpi)
BGP metrics: seq, log_type, peer_ip_src, afi/safi, ip_prefix, bgp_nexthop, as_path, comms, ecomms, origin, local_pref, rd, label, aigp
configuration: Per-daemon config file at /etc/pmacct/<daemon>.conf using key: value syntax; comments with '!'
plugins directive: comma-separated list with optional named instances, e.g. 'plugins: print[foo], kafka[bar]'
aggregate directive per plugin: defines which primitives to aggregate (src_host, dst_host, src_port, dst_port, proto, etc.)
aggregate_filter per plugin: BPF-style filter for selective aggregation
bgp_daemon_ip / bgp_daemon_port / bgp_daemon_max_peers for BGP peering configuration
SQL backends: --enable-mysql/pgsql/sqlite3 at compile time; table versioning required
Memory (IMT) plugin: imt_buckets, imt_mem_pools_size, imt_mem_pools_number, imt_path
CONFIG-KEYS file documents all configuration directives exhaustively
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection framework; pmacct is a passive collector only
Replication via tee plugin (nfacctd/sfacctd) allows redirecting flows to alternate collectors for testing
debug: true config key enables verbose logging for troubleshooting
modes: Collection mode: passive listener for NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow/BMP/BGP/Telemetry
Probe/export mode: pmacctd and uacctd can re-export captured packets as NetFlow v5/v9, IPFIX, or sFlow via nfprobe/sfprobe plugins
Replication mode: tee plugin in nfacctd/sfacctd replicates flows to third-party collectors
Memory (IMT) mode: in-memory table with CLI query access via pmacct client
Daemon mode: daemonize: true/false; default false
BGP HA mode: documented in docs/README_BGP_BMP_HA.md
constraints: uacctd (NFLOG) is Linux-only; pmacctd (libpcap) works cross-platform
SQL plugins (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite3), Kafka, AMQP, Avro, nDPI, ZMQ, Redis are all disabled by default and require compile-time --enable-* flags
Multi-platform Docker images (linux/arm64) are experimental and require an auxiliary registry for multi-platform builds
Memory (IMT) plugin is recommended only for prototyping and small-scale environments, not mass traffic
tee plugin is incompatible with other plugins in the same daemon instance
nfprobe and sfprobe plugins apply only to pmacctd and uacctd, not to nfacctd/sfacctd
gRPC/gNMI Streaming Telemetry requires --enable-grpc-collector and the external mdt-dialout-collector dependency
YANG Push/UDP-Notif requires --enable-unyte-udp-notif and the external udp-notif-c-collector dependency
BGP daemon listens on port 179 and requires router-side configuration to peer with pmacct's IP
docker_services: pmacct/nfacctd — NetFlow/IPFIX collector; default config at /etc/pmacct/nfacctd.conf; UDP port 2100 (example)
pmacct/sfacctd — sFlow collector; default config at /etc/pmacct/sfacctd.conf; UDP port 6343 (example)
pmacct/pmacctd — libpcap collector; default config at /etc/pmacct/pmacctd.conf
pmacct/pmbgpd — BGP collector; default config at /etc/pmacct/pmbgpd.conf
pmacct/pmbmpd — BMP collector; default config at /etc/pmacct/pmbmpd.conf
pmacct/pmtelemetryd — Streaming Telemetry collector; default config at /etc/pmacct/pmtelemetryd.conf
pmacct/uacctd — NFLOG collector (Linux only); default config at /etc/pmacct/uacctd.conf
All images are built from a shared base (debian:trixie-slim) with all plugins compiled in; tags: latest, vX.Y.Z, bleeding-edge
notable_absences: No built-in web UI or REST API — all output goes to files, databases, or message brokers
No docker-compose file committed to the repository; example compose config is only in docs/DOCKER.md
No native InfluxDB/Prometheus output plugin — Kafka/AMQP are the recommended bridges to those systems
No SNMP trap collection — pmacct does not support SNMP as an input protocol
No flow deduplication across replicated collectors out of the box
